anthropic/claude-opus-5-5.text:
verdict: needs-work
addresses-problem: yes — all four widgets ticket rows are carried verbatim and disposed `in-scope`, and the Design covers each one. The mailer row is `elsewhere: acme/mailer` and sits under the `### acme/mailer` repo-group heading, which names a repo other than acme/widgets, so that disposition is valid.
findings:
- [major] ambiguity @ Design: "the mailer handoff reuses the existing export-ready event" — The spec never says whether widgets emits this event, when it fires, or what the payload holds. Export is a synchronous `GET /widgets/export.csv`, so an "export-ready" moment is not defined. The mailer row needs "the download link", but the spec does not say who supplies that link or in what form. An implementer cannot tell whether widgets must publish anything. → State whether widgets publishes the export-ready event and at what point, for example on Export click or never. Name the payload fields, including the download URL (`/widgets/export.csv` or a signed variant). Add a Verification line asserting the emission, or state explicitly that widgets emits nothing. — probed: none
- [major] gap @ Verification: "Request tests check the download headers, column order and CSV escaping, and header-only empty output" — The Design puts the endpoint behind session authentication and limits it to the signed-in user's widgets. No test covers either property, so a cross-user data leak or unauthenticated access to a new data-export endpoint would go uncaught. → Add request tests asserting that an unauthenticated request is rejected or redirected. Add a test asserting that the CSV contains only the signed-in user's widgets when another user's widgets exist. — probed: none
- [minor] ambiguity @ Verification: "Run the 10000-widget benchmark for the 60s row when in-scope" — The row is already disposed `in-scope`, so the conditional is dead wording that could be read as optional. The spec also does not say whether the benchmark is an automated test, a CI job, or a manual run, or what environment it runs in beyond "local". → Replace with "Run the 10000-widget benchmark and assert the complete response arrives within 60s." Name where the benchmark lives and how it runs, for example a tagged test or a script path. — probed: none
- [minor] ambiguity @ Design: "Encode id, name, and status with standard CSV quoting" — "Standard" is not pinned to a definition. The spec leaves open the line terminator (CRLF vs LF), whether to emit a BOM, and how to render a null name or status. The escaping test cannot assert exact bytes without these. → Cite RFC 4180, choose a line terminator, state that there is no BOM (or that there is one), and say how null or empty values render. — probed: none
lean: nothing to cut
